## Notebook Overview

**Inputs:**

- US Census Bureau ACS 5-year API (via `tidycensus`): 2012–2016 ACS at the
  **tract** level and 2020–2024 ACS at the **block-group** level, California.
- `../../../data-raw-temp/nhgis/nhgis_bg2020_tr2010_06/nhgis_bg2020_tr2010_06.csv`
  — NHGIS geographic crosswalk, 2020 block groups → 2010 tracts (allocation weights).
- `../../../data-raw-temp/nhgis/nhgis_tr2000_tr2010_06/nhgis_tr2000_tr2010_06.csv`
  — NHGIS geographic crosswalk, 2000 tracts → 2010 tracts (allocation weights).

**Outputs:**

- `../../../data/acs_step1_16.feather` — 2012–2016 ACS estimates, one row per 2010 CA tract.
- `../../../data/acs_step1_24.feather` — 2020–2024 ACS estimates, one row per 2020 CA block group.
- `../../../data/xwalk_bg24_tr10.feather` — 2020 block group → 2010 tract crosswalk (weights).
- `../../../data/xwalk_tr00_tr10.feather` — 2000 tract → 2010 tract crosswalk (weights).

This notebook:

1. Sets up the environment (packages, helper functions, data paths)
2. Defines the target ACS variables to extract
3. Imports and prepares the 2012–2016 ACS tract data
4. Imports and prepares the 2020–2024 ACS block-group data
5. Imports and prepares the geographic crosswalks
6. Validates the saved outputs

This step only **imports and stores** source data; it performs no row-level
filtering or sample restriction. Geographic harmonization (aggregating the
2020–2024 block-group data to 2010 tracts using these crosswalks) happens in
`02_assemble.Rmd`.

## 1.2 Load helper functions

Reusable helpers (`rent_cat_sum()`, `summ_var()`, `rename_id()`, `save_data()`,
and the diagnostic helpers `report_n()` / `print_numeric_summary()`) live in
`R/helpers.R` and are loaded here. Keeping them in one documented file lets every
notebook in this stage share the same definitions.

```{r load-helpers}
source(here::here("R", "helpers.R"))
```

## 1.3 Set data paths

All paths are relative to this repository, which is the integration point
between pipeline stages. Raw source files are read from `../../../data-raw-temp/`
(never modified); processed outputs are written to `../../../data/`.

```{r set-paths}
# Trailing slash on data_dir is intentional: save_data() builds paths with paste0().
data_dir <- "../../../data/"
raw_dir  <- "../../../data-raw-temp"
```

# 2. Define target ACS variables

## 2.1 Load ACS variable dictionaries

The full ACS variable dictionaries are loaded for interactive lookup of Census
table/variable codes while selecting measures. They are not used in any
downstream transformation.

```{r load-variable-dictionaries}
v16 <- load_variables(2016, "acs5")
v24 <- load_variables(2024, "acs5")
```

## 2.2 Specify variables to extract

`v16_save` maps short, analysis-friendly names to Census variable codes. The
same set is reused for 2024 (`v24_save`) so the two vintages share an identical
variable layout. Inline comments give the plain-language meaning of each code.

This set includes vacancy-status detail from table B25004: `vac_forrent` (vacant
units for rent) and `vac_forsale` (vacant units for sale only).

# 3. Import and prepare 2012–2016 ACS tract data

## 3.1 Download 2016 ACS tract estimates

Pulls the selected variables for all California census tracts from the 2012–2016
ACS 5-year file in wide format (one column per estimate `*E` and margin of error
`*M`). Expected: one row per CA 2010-vintage tract (~8,057).

```{r download-acs-tract-16}
acs_trt_16 <- get_acs(geography = "tract",
                       state = "CA",
                       variables = v16_save,
                       year = 2016,
                       output = "wide",
                       survey = "acs5")

report_n(acs_trt_16, "2016 ACS tracts imported")
```

## 3.2 Derive low-rent housing-unit counts

### Decision: Year-specific low-rent category cutoffs

We build two aggregate "low rent" renter-occupied housing-unit counts by summing
contiguous gross-rent categories (table B25063). For **2016** we use categories
**1–17** (`rhu_lrE`) and **1–19** (`rhu_lr2E`).

**Rationale:**

- The gross-rent categories are fixed dollar bins that do not move with
  inflation, so the dollar value of a given "low rent" threshold drifts upward
  over time.
- To keep the *real* rent threshold roughly comparable across vintages, the
  2020–2024 cutoffs are shifted up by one category (1–18 / 1–20; see Section 4.2).

```{r derive-low-rent-16}
acs_trt_16 <- acs_trt_16 |>
  mutate(
    rhu_lrE  = rent_cat_sum(1, 17),
    rhu_lr2E = rent_cat_sum(1, 19)
  )
```

## 3.3 Check missingness and margins of error

Quick data-quality probe on two bellwether estimates (population and median
gross rent): counts, missingness, mean/range, and mean margin of error.

```{r check-missingness-16}
vars <- c("popE", "rentE")

out <- map_dfr(vars, ~summ_var(acs_trt_16, .x))
out
```

## 3.4 Rename geographic ID and save

Renames `GEOID` to `tr2010_id` (and tags the table with the `rent_id` join
flag), then writes the output. **Output:** `acs_step1_16.feather` — 2012–2016 ACS
estimates with one row per 2010 CA tract, consumed by `02_assemble.Rmd`.

```{r save-acs-tract-16}
acs_trt_16 <- rename_id(acs_trt_16, tr2010_id, GEOID)

report_n(acs_trt_16, "2016 ACS tracts saved")
save_data(acs_trt_16, data_dir, "acs_step1_16.feather")

rm(v16, v16_save)
```

# 4. Import and prepare 2020–2024 ACS block-group data

## 4.1 Download 2024 ACS block-group estimates

### Decision: Pull 2020–2024 at the block-group level

The 2020–2024 ACS is imported at the **block-group** level (not tract), because
2020-vintage block groups can be allocated to 2010 tracts using the NHGIS
crosswalk loaded in Section 5.1. Aggregation to 2010 tracts happens downstream in
`02_assemble.Rmd`. Expected: one row per CA 2020-vintage block group (~25,000+).

```{r download-acs-bg-23}
acs_bg_24 <- get_acs(geography = "block group",
                       state = "CA",
                       variables = v24_save,
                       year = 2024,
                       output = "wide",
                       survey = "acs5")

report_n(acs_bg_24, "2024 ACS block groups imported")

# # These rely on calc_cv()/calc_pct() helpers and are computed downstream instead.

#          rentCV = calc_cv(rentE, rentM),
#          pctrhu = calc_pct(rhuE, rhu_baseE),
#          pctvac = calc_pct(tot_vacE, tot_vac_baseE),

#          pctaa = calc_pct(pop_aaE, pop_raceE),
#          pcthsp = calc_pct(pop_hspE, pop_raceE),
#          pctsfd = calc_pct(sfd_detE, sfd_baseE),
#          rhu_lrE = rent_cat_sum(1,18),
#          rhu_lr2E = rent_cat_sum(1,20)
#          )
```

## 4.2 Derive low-rent housing-unit counts

### Decision: Shift low-rent cutoffs up one category for 2020–2024

For **2024** we use gross-rent categories **1–18** (`rhu_lrE`) and **1–20**
(`rhu_lr2E`) — one category higher than the 2016 cutoffs (Section 3.2) — to hold
the real (inflation-adjusted) low-rent threshold roughly constant across vintages.

```{r derive-low-rent-23}
acs_bg_24 <- acs_bg_24 |>
  mutate(
    rhu_lrE  = rent_cat_sum(1, 18),
    rhu_lr2E = rent_cat_sum(1, 20)
  )
```

## 4.3 Check missingness and margins of error

Same bellwether data-quality probe as Section 3.3, on the block-group data.

```{r check-missingness-23}
vars <- c("popE", "rentE")

out <- map_dfr(vars, ~summ_var(acs_bg_24, .x))
out
```

## 4.4 Rename geographic ID and save

Renames `GEOID` to `bg2020_id` (and tags the `rent_id` flag), then writes the
output. **Output:** `acs_step1_24.feather` — 2020–2024 ACS estimates with one row
per 2020 CA block group, consumed by `02_assemble.Rmd`.

```{r save-acs-bg-23}
acs_bg_24 <- rename_id(acs_bg_24, bg2020_id, GEOID)

report_n(acs_bg_24, "2024 ACS block groups saved")
save_data(acs_bg_24, data_dir, "acs_step1_24.feather")

rm(v24, v24_save)
```

# 5. Import and prepare geographic crosswalks

## 5.1 Crosswalk 2024 block groups to 2010 tracts

### Decision: Use NHGIS weighted crosswalks for geographic harmonization

We use the NHGIS block-group-to-tract crosswalk, which provides allocation
weights (`wt_pop`, `wt_hh`, `wt_hu`, `wt_renthu`) giving the share of each source
geography's population / households / housing units / renter housing units that
falls into each target tract. Downstream aggregation (`02_assemble.Rmd`) uses
these weights to apportion block-group estimates to 2010 tracts.

Because a single block group can split across multiple tracts (and vice versa),
the crosswalk is intentionally **many-to-many**: the unique row key is the
(`bg2020_id`, `tr2010_id`) pair, not either ID alone.

```{r import-xwalk-bg-tr}
xwalk <- read_csv(file.path(raw_dir, "nhgis", "nhgis_bg2020_tr2010_06",
                            "nhgis_bg2020_tr2010_06.csv")) |>
  mutate(x_id = TRUE)

report_n(xwalk, "bg2020->tr2010 crosswalk imported")

# Missing-data check on the weight columns
xwalk |>
  summarise(
    across(c(wt_pop, wt_hh), list(
      n = ~sum(!is.na(.)),
      pct_missing = ~100 * sum(is.na(.)) / n(),
      mean = ~mean(., na.rm = TRUE),
      min = ~min(., na.rm = TRUE),
      max = ~max(., na.rm = TRUE)
    ),
    .names = "{.col}_{.fn}")
  )

xwalk |>
  summarise(
    across(c(wt_hu, wt_renthu), list(
      n = ~sum(!is.na(.)),
      pct_missing = ~100 * sum(is.na(.)) / n(),
      mean = ~mean(., na.rm = TRUE),
      min = ~min(., na.rm = TRUE),
      max = ~max(., na.rm = TRUE)
    ),
    .names = "{.col}_{.fn}")
  )

# Key check: rows should be unique on the (block group, tract) pair.
# Duplicate block-group IDs are EXPECTED here (split block groups).
cat(sprintf(
  "bg2020->tr2010: %s rows | %s unique (bg, tract) pairs | %s block groups | %s tracts\n",
  formatC(nrow(xwalk), format = "d", big.mark = ","),
  formatC(n_distinct(xwalk$bg2020ge, xwalk$tr2010ge), format = "d", big.mark = ","),
  formatC(n_distinct(xwalk$bg2020ge), format = "d", big.mark = ","),
  formatC(n_distinct(xwalk$tr2010ge), format = "d", big.mark = ",")
))

# Rename to pipeline ID names and keep only key + weight columns
xwalk <- xwalk |>
  rename(bg2020_id = bg2020ge,
         tr2010_id = tr2010ge) |>
  select(c(bg2020_id, tr2010_id, wt_pop, wt_hh, wt_hu, wt_renthu, x_id))

# Output: xwalk_bg24_tr10.feather — 2020 block group -> 2010 tract weights
report_n(xwalk, "bg2020->tr2010 crosswalk saved")
xwalk |>
  arrow::write_feather(paste0(data_dir, "xwalk_bg24_tr10.feather"))

rm(xwalk)
```

## 5.2 Crosswalk 2000 tracts to 2010 tracts

The NHGIS 2000-tract-to-2010-tract crosswalk, used to harmonize 2000-vintage
tract geographies to 2010 tracts. As in Section 5.1 the crosswalk is
many-to-many, keyed on the (`tr2000_id`, `tr2010_id`) pair.

```{r import-xwalk-tr-tr}
xwalk <- read_csv(file.path(raw_dir, "nhgis", "nhgis_tr2000_tr2010_06",
                            "nhgis_tr2000_tr2010_06.csv")) |>
  mutate(x_id = TRUE)

report_n(xwalk, "tr2000->tr2010 crosswalk imported")

# Missing-data check on the weight columns
xwalk |>
  summarise(
    across(c(wt_pop, wt_hh), list(
      n = ~sum(!is.na(.)),
      pct_missing = ~100 * sum(is.na(.)) / n(),
      mean = ~mean(., na.rm = TRUE),
      min = ~min(., na.rm = TRUE),
      max = ~max(., na.rm = TRUE)
    ),
    .names = "{.col}_{.fn}")
  )

xwalk |>
  summarise(
    across(c(wt_hu, wt_renthu), list(
      n = ~sum(!is.na(.)),
      pct_missing = ~100 * sum(is.na(.)) / n(),
      mean = ~mean(., na.rm = TRUE),
      min = ~min(., na.rm = TRUE),
      max = ~max(., na.rm = TRUE)
    ),
    .names = "{.col}_{.fn}")
  )

# Key check: rows should be unique on the (2000 tract, 2010 tract) pair.
# Duplicate 2000-tract IDs are EXPECTED here (split tracts).
cat(sprintf(
  "tr2000->tr2010: %s rows | %s unique (tr2000, tr2010) pairs | %s 2000 tracts | %s 2010 tracts\n",
  formatC(nrow(xwalk), format = "d", big.mark = ","),
  formatC(n_distinct(xwalk$tr2000ge, xwalk$tr2010ge), format = "d", big.mark = ","),
  formatC(n_distinct(xwalk$tr2000ge), format = "d", big.mark = ","),
  formatC(n_distinct(xwalk$tr2010ge), format = "d", big.mark = ",")
))

# Rename to pipeline ID names and keep only key + weight columns
xwalk <- xwalk |>
  rename(tr2000_id = tr2000ge,
         tr2010_id = tr2010ge) |>
  select(c(tr2000_id, tr2010_id, wt_pop, wt_hh, wt_hu, wt_renthu, x_id))

# Output: xwalk_tr00_tr10.feather — 2000 tract -> 2010 tract weights
report_n(xwalk, "tr2000->tr2010 crosswalk saved")
xwalk |>
  arrow::write_feather(paste0(data_dir, "xwalk_tr00_tr10.feather"))

rm(xwalk)
```

# 6. Validate outputs

This section re-loads the four saved outputs from `../../../data/` and checks
each for key uniqueness, missingness on critical variables, the encoding of the
join-flag columns, and the distribution (mean / range) of every numeric column.
Re-reading the written files confirms the save round-tripped correctly.

```{r reload-outputs}
acs16_out <- arrow::read_feather(paste0(data_dir, "acs_step1_16.feather"))
acs24_out <- arrow::read_feather(paste0(data_dir, "acs_step1_24.feather"))
xbg_out   <- arrow::read_feather(paste0(data_dir, "xwalk_bg24_tr10.feather"))
xtr_out   <- arrow::read_feather(paste0(data_dir, "xwalk_tr00_tr10.feather"))
```

## 6.1 Check key uniqueness and duplicates

Expected: the ACS tables are unique on their geographic ID; the crosswalks are
unique on their (source, target) key pair (individual source/target IDs repeat
by design).

```{r validate-keys}
cat("acs_step1_16: ", nrow(acs16_out), "rows |",
    n_distinct(acs16_out$tr2010_id), "unique tr2010_id |",
    sum(duplicated(acs16_out$tr2010_id)), "duplicate ids\n")

cat("acs_step1_24: ", nrow(acs24_out), "rows |",
    n_distinct(acs24_out$bg2020_id), "unique bg2020_id |",
    sum(duplicated(acs24_out$bg2020_id)), "duplicate ids\n")

cat("xwalk_bg24_tr10: ", nrow(xbg_out), "rows |",
    n_distinct(xbg_out$bg2020_id, xbg_out$tr2010_id), "unique (bg, tract) pairs |",
    sum(duplicated(xbg_out[c("bg2020_id", "tr2010_id")])), "duplicate pairs\n")

cat("xwalk_tr00_tr10: ", nrow(xtr_out), "rows |",
    n_distinct(xtr_out$tr2000_id, xtr_out$tr2010_id), "unique (tr2000, tr2010) pairs |",
    sum(duplicated(xtr_out[c("tr2000_id", "tr2010_id")])), "duplicate pairs\n")
```

## 6.2 Check missingness on critical variables

Expected: no missing geographic IDs. Some missingness in median rent (`rentE`)
is expected for sparsely-renter-occupied geographies; we report the counts rather
than impose a threshold here.

```{r validate-missingness}
cat("acs_step1_16 missing tr2010_id:", sum(is.na(acs16_out$tr2010_id)), "\n")
cat("acs_step1_16 missing rentE:    ", sum(is.na(acs16_out$rentE)), "\n")
cat("acs_step1_24 missing bg2020_id:", sum(is.na(acs24_out$bg2020_id)), "\n")
cat("acs_step1_24 missing rentE:    ", sum(is.na(acs24_out$rentE)), "\n")

cat("xwalk_bg24_tr10 missing keys:",
    sum(is.na(xbg_out$bg2020_id) | is.na(xbg_out$tr2010_id)), "\n")
cat("xwalk_tr00_tr10 missing keys:",
    sum(is.na(xtr_out$tr2000_id) | is.na(xtr_out$tr2010_id)), "\n")
```

## 6.3 Check flag-variable encoding

The join flags (`rent_id`, `x_id`) should be logical `TRUE`/`FALSE`, not string
labels. Expected: class `logical` for each.

```{r validate-flags}
cat("acs_step1_16 rent_id class:", class(acs16_out$rent_id),
    "| values:", paste(unique(acs16_out$rent_id), collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("acs_step1_24 rent_id class:", class(acs24_out$rent_id),
    "| values:", paste(unique(acs24_out$rent_id), collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("xwalk_bg24_tr10 x_id class:", class(xbg_out$x_id),
    "| values:", paste(unique(xbg_out$x_id), collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("xwalk_tr00_tr10 x_id class:", class(xtr_out$x_id),
    "| values:", paste(unique(xtr_out$x_id), collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

## 6.4 Summarize numeric variable distributions

Mean, min, and max for every numeric column in each output. Watch for impossible
values (negative counts, weights outside [0, 1], or estimates far outside
plausible ACS ranges).
